purpose: Persist source findings used to verify Veien Kulturminnepark's coordinate, identity, archaeological chronology, component boundaries and access context.

legacyCoordinate.assessment: Unsupported point approximately 2026.7 metres north-east of the named heritage park.

identityResolution.entityType: archaeological heritage park with burial field, reconstructed longhouse and museum building

supports: over one hundred visible burial mounds
free outdoor burial-field access under normal conditions
main grave chronology from the beginning of the Common Era to about 400
47-metre longhouse from the Early Roman Iron Age

chronology.event: Settlement traces include multiple longhouses, including a roughly 47-metre building from the Early Roman Iron Age.
The main burial-field and rich-grave phase developed, with some later finds also present.
The burial field was recorded with 144 mounds.
Oluf Rygh systematically investigated and documented many of the burial mounds.
A longhouse was reconstructed as an interpretation building based on excavated local settlement traces.

interpretationLimits: The canonical coordinate represents the heritage park as a whole through its named museum point.
The point does not define the protected burial-field boundary.
The reconstructed longhouse is a modern interpretation building, not an original surviving Iron Age structure.
Year 200 is an approximate archaeological anchor, not a single construction, burial or institution date.
The museum building, burial field and longhouse are distinct components with different access conditions.
The existing desc and popupDesc remain unchanged under place-description governance.
